title: The Church in medieval life
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:19Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point, his-christianity-medieval-europe, covers the Church's role in daily life, learning, politics and wealth, but it does not mention the Church running hospitals or its power rivalling the king's, which the brief requires, so a new point is the safer match.

draft.title: The Church in medieval life
card: In medieval Europe, most people were Catholic. The Catholic Church was part of everyday life from birth to death, with baptisms, weddings and funerals.
The Church ran many schools and hospitals. Monks and nuns often did this work, and they cared for the sick and taught people to read.
The Church collected a tithe from its people. A tithe was a tenth of a person's produce or income, paid to support the Church and its priests.
The Church owned a lot of land and had great influence. Its power sometimes rivalled the king's, so kings and Church leaders could clash.
draft.remember: The Church shaped daily life, ran services, took a tithe and could rival kings.

a.q: A peasant family in medieval England gives a tenth of their harvest to the local priest. What is this payment called?
opts: A tax paid to the king
A fee for a hospital stay
A rent paid to the lord
a.why: A tithe was a tenth of produce or income paid to the Church. It was not paid to the king, and it was not a fee for a hospital stay, because those were run by the Church as a service.
a.clue: Who received the harvest share, the king or the Church?

b.q: In a medieval town, a boy learns to read from monks and a sick neighbour is cared for by nuns. What does this best show about the Church?
opts: It provided services that shaped daily life
It had no influence outside church services
It was controlled by the local king
It only dealt with rich nobles
b.why: Schools and hospitals run by monks and nuns show the Church provided services in daily life. It was not limited to church services, because it also taught and cared for people from all kinds of families.
b.clue: Think about what monks and nuns did beyond prayer.

b.best: It provided services that shaped daily life
